newsitem.title: USA: Nazi list of looted Jewish art collections found.
newsitem.headline: Nazi list of looted Jewish art collections found.

text.p: The Nazis' own list of the Jewish art collections they looted in France has been found in the U.S. National Archives and has been sent to the French Jewish community, the World Jewish Congress said on Tuesday.

The list of 79 collections was compiled by Hitler's henchman Alfred Rosenberg, who personally oversaw the looting of art that belonged to such famous collectors as the Rothschilds, the Wildensteins and David Weill.
It was found in a collection of Office of Strategic Services papers at the National Archives, the WJC said. The OSS was the forerunner of the Central Intelligence Agency.
Five of the collections on the list contained 21,903 items, said WJC Vice President Kalman Sultanilk, who added, "some were returned, some were not."
He said the collections would be worth hundreds of millions of dollars today and contained many great works of art, including impressionist and old Master paintings.
France this week announced the formation of a committee to identify property stolen from Jews during the war. The property is believed to include 2,000 works of art in French museums.
The head of the French museums network protested against accusations that it had intentionally not identified the owners of the 2,000 works of art.

Francoise Cachin said that of 60,000 works of art recovered by France from the Nazis after the war, 45,000 were returned to their rightful owners or heirs, 15,000 that were of little value were sold and only 2,000 remained under "provisional administration."
The works of art have drawn special attention because they included priceless items by Gauguin, Renoir and Rodin.

Cachin told French television that she believed most of the 2,000 remaining paintings and sculptures, which are on show in museums around the country, were never claimed "because they were not stolen during the occupation but sold."
